I also feel so embarrassed about how I look and eat that I turn down social invitations, and the emotional weight of missing my mom just makes everything feel much more draining.\n\nDoctor: Is the decrease in pleasure you're experiencing from activities like volunteering and hiking more related to your physical condition and guilt over eating, or do you feel a general disinterest in activities that you normally find enjoyable?\n\nPatient: It is definitely more about my physical limitations and the shame I feel, rather than a loss of interest. I still truly want to do my volunteering and hiking, but getting winded so easily and feeling so embarrassed about my weight makes it incredibly hard to actually go out and enjoy them.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing or have no interest in doing anymore, that aren't affected by your physical condition or weight?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, because the main activities I've stepped back from, like hiking or going to social gatherings, are directly related to my physical stamina or feeling embarrassed about my weight and eating. I still try to keep up with volunteering and my quilting circle when I can, because I still care about them.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you've completely lost interest in, separate from the physical difficulties or feelings of embarrassment you've mentioned, that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing and the start of these eating episodes?\n\nPatient: I don't think I've completely lost interest in my hobbies like gardening or quilting. Because of that, I don't really have a specific recent experience of trying them to share with you.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's anything you used to enjoy that you've completely stopped doing because you no longer find joy in it, not because of your physical condition or feelings of guilt and shame?\n\nPatient: No, there isn't anything I've stopped doing because I've lost interest in it. I still care deeply about quilting, gardening, and volunteering, but I've only pulled back because I'm physically exhausted, self-conscious about my weight, or because the grief of losing my mom makes them feel too painful right now. It's not that the activities themselves have lost their joy, it's just everything else around them that makes it hard.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times recently when you were able to engage in one of your usual activities without feeling physically limited or self-conscious, and if so, did you feel a sense of pleasure or enjoyment during that time?\n\nPatient: Unfortunately, it has been very difficult to find moments like that lately. Hiking now quickly leaves me feeling winded and tired, and volunteering at the food bank has become exhausting. I've also been turning down social invites, like with my quilting circle, because I feel too self-conscious about my weight and appearance to enjoy myself.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you've been able to participate in recently without feeling physically limited or self-conscious, and if so, did you still feel a lack of enjoyment or pleasure during those times?\n\nPatient: It's really hard for me to think of any activities lately where I don't feel at least somewhat physically limited or self-conscious. Between getting winded so easily and feeling so embarrassed about my appearance, almost everything I do feels affected right now. Because of that, I'm not really sure how to answer whether I've had any moments without those limitations.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you've lost interest in over time, separate from the physical difficulties or feelings of embarrassment you've mentioned, that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing?"

It's just that doing them now feels very empty and quiet without my mother there to share them with me.\n\nDoctor: Are you experiencing a lack of interest in activities that you normally enjoy, separate from the feelings of guilt, shame, or physical limitations you've mentioned, and if so, can you give me an example?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't actually lost interest in the things I love, like gardening, quilting, or hiking. I still really want to do them, but I find myself avoiding them or struggling solely because I get winded so easily now, or because I feel too embarrassed about my weight to be around other people.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's a specific activity that you used to enjoy, which you now engage in without feeling any pleasure, not because of physical limitations or feelings of guilt, but simply because the activity itself no longer brings you joy?\n\nPatient: I haven't really experienced that, doctor. I still truly want to do my quilting and volunteering, but I just feel too physically tired or too embarrassed about my weight to actually go out and do them. The activities themselves haven't lost their joy; it's just my own exhaustion and self-consciousness holding me back.\n\nDoctor: Is there anything that suggests your lack of enjoyment in activities is due to a genuine loss of interest in them, rather than the physical and emotional challenges you're currently facing?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely the physical and emotional challenges keeping me back rather than a loss of interest. I still want to hike and see my friends, but getting winded easily from my weight gain, combined with feeling embarrassed and exhausted by my eating habits and grief, makes it too hard to participate.\n\nDoctor: If your physical health and emotional state were to suddenly improve, do you think you would regain your previous level of enjoyment and interest in activities like hiking, volunteering, and quilting?\n\nPatient: Oh, I would absolutely love to get back to those activities because I deeply miss hiking, volunteering, and my quilting circle, especially since quilting and gardening were things I shared so closely with my mother. Right now, the physical exhaustion, getting winded from my weight gain, and the deep shame over how I look are the main barriers holding me back. If those improved, I really hope I would find that joy and connection again.\n\nDoctor: If you were able to participate in your favorite activities without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, do you think you would still feel a lack of pleasure or enjoyment, or would you expect to feel the same level of enjoyment as you did before your mother's passing and the start of your eating episodes?\n\nPatient: That is a really difficult question to answer because the grief, shame, and physical struggles are all so tangled up right now. Since my mother's absence still leaves such a huge emptiness, I'm not sure if I would enjoy things the same way, but I honestly don't know how I would feel without the constant physical exhaustion and embarrassment.\n\nDoctor: Can you imagine a situation where you're participating in one of your favorite activities, like quilting or hiking, without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, and in that scenario, do you think you would feel a genuine sense of pleasure and enjoyment, or would something still be missing for you?"

Even while a little voice in my head is telling me to stop because I'll feel sick, my hands just keep reaching and I can't seem to put the fork down.\n\nDoctor: During these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you feel a sense of guilt, shame, or self-criticism afterwards?\n\nPatient: Yes, I feel terribly guilty and ashamed afterward. I'll sit in the quiet kitchen staring at the empty pans and wrappers, just beating myself up for doing it again. It makes me feel so down, especially since my clothes don't fit anymore and I can't even go hiking like I used to.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your interest in sex or your sexual performance around the same time you started experiencing these nighttime eating episodes?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any changes in that area, to be honest. It hasn't really been on my mind at all, especially since my mother passed away.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling down after these eating episodes and also mentioned your mother passing away; have you been feeling consistently sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, since your mother's passing?\n\nPatient: No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or sad all day long, because I still have the energy to go volunteer at the food bank and visit the farmer's market. But a deep emptiness really hits me when I come back to a quiet house without my mother, and the worst feelings of guilt and shame happen right after those late-night eating episodes.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned still having the energy to volunteer and visit the market, but have you noticed any decrease in the pleasure you get from these activities or other things you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: I still want to do those things and haven't lost interest, but they've become much harder to actually enjoy. Volunteering feels so much more exhausting now, and I get winded easily on hikes I used to love. I've even started turning down social invitations because I feel so embarrassed about my weight gain and how I've been eating.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'they've become much harder to actually enjoy' when it comes to volunteering and other activities, and is this feeling of not enjoying things as much related to your weight gain, the eating episodes, or something else entirely?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is mostly due to the physical toll of the weight I've gained—I get winded so quickly on hikes now, and my volunteer shifts at the food bank feel physically exhausting. I also feel so embarrassed about how I look and eat that I turn down social invitations, and the emotional weight of missing my mom just makes everything feel much more draining.\n\nDoctor: Is the decrease in pleasure you're experiencing from activities like volunteering and hiking more related to your physical condition and guilt over eating, or do you feel a general disinterest in activities that you normally find enjoyable?\n\nPatient: It is definitely more about my physical limitations and the shame I feel, rather than a loss of interest. I still truly want to do my volunteering and hiking, but getting winded so easily and feeling so embarrassed about my weight makes it incredibly hard to actually go out and enjoy them.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing or have no interest in doing anymore, that aren't affected by your physical condition or weight?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, because the main activities I've stepped back from, like hiking or going to social gatherings, are directly related to my physical stamina or feeling embarrassed about my weight and eating. I still try to keep up with volunteering and my quilting circle when I can, because I still care about them.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you've completely lost interest in, separate from the physical difficulties or feelings of embarrassment you've mentioned, that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing and the start of these eating episodes?\n\nPatient: I don't think I've completely lost interest in my hobbies like gardening or quilting. It's just been very hard to find the energy or motivation to do them since my mother passed away, rather than a total loss of interest.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned it's hard to find energy or motivation for activities like gardening or quilting since your mother passed away, but can you think of any specific times or situations when you did try to engage in these activities and how you felt during or after doing them?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I haven't really been able to bring myself to do much gardening or quilting since my mother passed away because those activities feel too empty and painful without her. Because of that, I don't really have a specific recent experience of trying them to share with you.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's anything you used to enjoy that you've completely stopped doing because you no longer find joy in it, not because of your physical condition or feelings of guilt and shame?\n\nPatient: No, there isn't anything I've stopped doing because I've lost interest in it. I still care deeply about quilting, gardening, and volunteering, but I've only pulled back because I'm physically exhausted, self-conscious about my weight, or because the grief of losing my mom makes them feel too painful right now. It's not that the activities themselves have lost their joy, it's just everything else around them that makes it hard.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times recently when you were able to engage in one of your usual activities without feeling physically limited or self-conscious, and if so, did you feel a sense of pleasure or enjoyment during that time?\n\nPatient: Unfortunately, it has been very difficult to find moments like that lately. Hiking now quickly leaves me feeling winded and tired, and volunteering at the food bank has become exhausting. I've also been turning down social invites, like with my quilting circle, because I feel too self-conscious about my weight and appearance to enjoy myself.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you've been able to participate in recently without feeling physically limited or self-conscious, and if so, did you still feel a lack of enjoyment or pleasure during those times?\n\nPatient: It's really hard for me to think of any activities lately where I don't feel at least somewhat physically limited or self-conscious. Between getting winded so easily and feeling so embarrassed about my appearance, almost everything I do feels affected right now. Because of that, I'm not really sure how to answer whether I've had any moments without those limitations.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you've lost interest in over time, separate from the physical difficulties or feelings of embarrassment you've mentioned, that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing?\n\nPatient: I haven't really lost interest in my favorite activities like quilting or gardening. It's just that doing them now feels very empty and quiet without my mother there to share them with me.\n\nDoctor: Are you experiencing a lack of interest in activities that you normally enjoy, separate from the feelings of guilt, shame, or physical limitations you've mentioned, and if so, can you give me an example?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't actually lost interest in the things I love, like gardening, quilting, or hiking. I still really want to do them, but I find myself avoiding them or struggling solely because I get winded so easily now, or because I feel too embarrassed about my weight to be around other people.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's a specific activity that you used to enjoy, which you now engage in without feeling any pleasure, not because of physical limitations or feelings of guilt, but simply because the activity itself no longer brings you joy?\n\nPatient: I haven't really experienced that, doctor. I still truly want to do my quilting and volunteering, but I just feel too physically tired or too embarrassed about my weight to actually go out and do them. The activities themselves haven't lost their joy; it's just my own exhaustion and self-consciousness holding me back.\n\nDoctor: Is there anything that suggests your lack of enjoyment in activities is due to a genuine loss of interest in them, rather than the physical and emotional challenges you're currently facing?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely the physical and emotional challenges keeping me back rather than a loss of interest. I still want to hike and see my friends, but getting winded easily from my weight gain, combined with feeling embarrassed and exhausted by my eating habits and grief, makes it too hard to participate.\n\nDoctor: If your physical health and emotional state were to suddenly improve, do you think you would regain your previous level of enjoyment and interest in activities like hiking, volunteering, and quilting?\n\nPatient: Oh, I would absolutely love to get back to those activities because I deeply miss hiking, volunteering, and my quilting circle, especially since quilting and gardening were things I shared so closely with my mother. Right now, the physical exhaustion, getting winded from my weight gain, and the deep shame over how I look are the main barriers holding me back. If those improved, I really hope I would find that joy and connection again.\n\nDoctor: If you were able to participate in your favorite activities without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, do you think you would still feel a lack of pleasure or enjoyment, or would you expect to feel the same level of enjoyment as you did before your mother's passing and the start of your eating episodes?\n\nPatient: That is a really difficult question to answer because the grief, shame, and physical struggles are all so tangled up right now. Since my mother's absence still leaves such a huge emptiness, I'm not sure if I would enjoy things the same way, but I honestly don't know how I would feel without the constant physical exhaustion and embarrassment.\n\nDoctor: Can you imagine a situation where you're participating in one of your favorite activities, like quilting or hiking, without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, and in that scenario, do you think you would feel a genuine sense of pleasure and enjoyment, or would something still be missing for you?\n\nPatient: While being free of the physical limitations and guilt would be a massive relief, I think a deep emptiness would still be there. Activities like quilting and gardening are so closely tied to my mother that even if my physical health and eating were perfect, I would still feel the painful void of her absence.\n\nDoctor: If you were to imagine yourself in a scenario where you've overcome your eating issues, your physical health has improved, and you're no longer feeling guilty or ashamed, would you expect to find genuine pleasure and enjoyment in activities like quilting, hiking, or volunteering, or do you think something would still be holding you back from feeling the way you used to?\n\nPatient: That is a very difficult question to answer, and I'm really not sure. I still really want to do them, but I find myself avoiding them or struggling solely because I get winded so easily now, or because I feel too embarrassed about my weight to be around other people.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's a specific activity that you used to enjoy, which you now engage in without feeling any pleasure, not because of physical limitations or feelings of guilt, but simply because the activity itself no longer brings you joy?\n\nPatient: I haven't really experienced that, doctor. I still truly want to do my quilting and volunteering, but I just feel too physically tired or too embarrassed about my weight to actually go out and do them. The activities themselves haven't lost their joy; it's just my own exhaustion and self-consciousness holding me back.\n\nDoctor: Is there anything that suggests your lack of enjoyment in activities is due to a genuine loss of interest in them, rather than the physical and emotional challenges you're currently facing?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely the physical and emotional challenges keeping me back rather than a loss of interest. I still want to hike and see my friends, but getting winded easily from my weight gain, combined with feeling embarrassed and exhausted by my eating habits and grief, makes it too hard to participate.\n\nDoctor: If your physical health and emotional state were to suddenly improve, do you think you would regain your previous level of enjoyment and interest in activities like hiking, volunteering, and quilting?\n\nPatient: Oh, I would absolutely love to get back to those activities because I deeply miss hiking, volunteering, and my quilting circle, especially since quilting and gardening were things I shared so closely with my mother. Hiking now quickly leaves me feeling winded and tired, and volunteering at the food bank has become exhausting. I've also been turning down social invites, like with my quilting circle, because I feel too self-conscious about my weight and appearance to enjoy myself.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you've been able to participate in recently without feeling physically limited or self-conscious, and if so, did you still feel a lack of enjoyment or pleasure during those times?\n\nPatient: It's really hard for me to think of any activities lately where I don't feel at least somewhat physically limited or self-conscious. Between getting winded so easily and feeling so embarrassed about my appearance, almost everything I do feels affected right now. Because of that, I'm not really sure how to answer whether I've had any moments without those limitations.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you've lost interest in over time, separate from the physical difficulties or feelings of embarrassment you've mentioned, that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing?\n\nPatient: I haven't really lost interest in my favorite activities like quilting or gardening. It's just that doing them now feels very empty and quiet without my mother there to share them with me.\n\nDoctor: Are you experiencing a lack of interest in activities that you normally enjoy, separate from the feelings of guilt, shame, or physical limitations you've mentioned, and if so, can you give me an example?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't actually lost interest in the things I love, like gardening, quilting, or hiking. I still really want to do them, but I find myself avoiding them or struggling solely because I get winded so easily now, or because I feel too embarrassed about my weight to be around other people.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there's a specific activity that you used to enjoy, which you now engage in without feeling any pleasure, not because of physical limitations or feelings of guilt, but simply because the activity itself no longer brings you joy?\n\nPatient: I haven't really experienced that, doctor. I still truly want to do my quilting and volunteering, but I just feel too physically tired or too embarrassed about my weight to actually go out and do them. The activities themselves haven't lost their joy; it's just my own exhaustion and self-consciousness holding me back.\n\nDoctor: Is there anything that suggests your lack of enjoyment in activities is due to a genuine loss of interest in them, rather than the physical and emotional challenges you're currently facing?\n\nPatient: No, it is definitely the physical and emotional challenges keeping me back rather than a loss of interest. I still want to hike and see my friends, but getting winded easily from my weight gain, combined with feeling embarrassed and exhausted by my eating habits and grief, makes it too hard to participate.\n\nDoctor: If your physical health and emotional state were to suddenly improve, do you think you would regain your previous level of enjoyment and interest in activities like hiking, volunteering, and quilting?\n\nPatient: Oh, I would absolutely love to get back to those activities because I deeply miss hiking, volunteering, and my quilting circle, especially since quilting and gardening were things I shared so closely with my mother. Right now, the physical exhaustion, getting winded from my weight gain, and the deep shame over how I look are the main barriers holding me back. If those improved, I really hope I would find that joy and connection again.\n\nDoctor: If you were able to participate in your favorite activities without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, do you think you would still feel a lack of pleasure or enjoyment, or would you expect to feel the same level of enjoyment as you did before your mother's passing and the start of your eating episodes?\n\nPatient: That is a really difficult question to answer because the grief, shame, and physical struggles are all so tangled up right now. Since my mother's absence still leaves such a huge emptiness, I'm not sure if I would enjoy things the same way, but I honestly don't know how I would feel without the constant physical exhaustion and embarrassment.\n\nDoctor: Can you imagine a situation where you're participating in one of your favorite activities, like quilting or hiking, without any physical limitations or feelings of guilt and shame, and in that scenario, do you think you would feel a genuine sense of pleasure and enjoyment, or would something still be missing for you?\n\nPatient: While being free of the physical limitations and guilt would be a massive relief, I think a deep emptiness would still be there. While those things would likely improve, the deep grief of losing my mother would probably still leave a sense of emptiness that I'd need to work through.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities that you used to find enjoyable before your mother's passing and the start of your eating episodes, that you still find enjoyable now, despite your current physical and emotional challenges?\n\nPatient: I still find some comfort in quilting, volunteering at the food bank, and church activities, since they keep me going and remind me of my mother.
